body:
# [wildcard] Cancellation is not completion: checked settlement for own-handle task regions

## The idea, in a paragraph

Add an opt-in structured task region for existing `own` handles: cancellation requests settlement; it never counts as completion. A region may return `Settled` only when every registered child has been joined and every registered input handle has exactly one terminal outcome: ownership transferred into its returned result bundle, or synchronous release completed. No child may retain that handle afterward. Start with a fixed finite child set, one handle per child, no nested spawning, outstanding borrows or escapes to globals, opaque callbacks or unverified containers. This is a proposed resource-accounting contract, not implemented behavior or a soundness-bug report.

## Which assumption it breaks

Fire-and-forget spawning need not be the only checked concurrency surface. Keep ordinary `task` unchanged; let users opt into a region whose exit accounts for ownership obligations. [C1](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/44a08b96dca77e49cf8c6469d8c177ef908b5234/SPEC-LANGUAGE.md#L1158) supplies no join handle, while [GUARANTEES rows 12/16](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/blob/44a08b96dca77e49cf8c6469d8c177ef908b5234/GUARANTEES.md#L53) leave cancellation and protocol ordering unmodeled. Go's [CancelFunc contract](https://pkg.go.dev/context#CancelFunc) also distinguishes requesting cancellation from waiting for work to stop.

## Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

The proposed change makes completion an ownership boundary: a caller receives either its handles back or evidence that their release actually finished, including on early return. It retains the borrow checker rather than replacing it. Unlike [#184](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/184), which excludes cancellation, it makes no deadlock-freedom claim; unlike [#174](https://github.com/limitlessprojects/Go-Hybrid/issues/174), it does not encode the general borrow checker into Go types. This addresses solicitation 4 with a deliberately narrow cancellation contract. Structured concurrency and affine obligations are established ideas; I claim no global novelty.

A generated region-local ledger tracks each obligation. Preparing a handoff escrows the handle and makes it unavailable to its sender. One atomic transition decides acquisition versus cancellation-before-acquisition. If acquisition wins, only the child can settle; cancellation cannot reclaim its live handle. If cancellation wins, acquisition is forbidden and the pending obligation still requires return or release. Only generated operations may produce affine terminal receipts, after transfer or release completes; receipt identifiers alone prove nothing. Parent early return first cancels and joins, then releases unconsumed returned handles. Incomplete cleanup prevents `Settled`.

## How we would know it works (or doesn't)

Before syntax work, enumerate a finite two-child model with one handle each and one pending handoff slot. Require positive traces for success, cancellation before acquisition, cooperative cancellation after acquisition, and parent early return. A permanently blocked child must remain unsettled, even after returning or releasing its handle.

One trace refutes the contract if `Settled` occurs with a missing handle, duplicate owner, child-retained handle or release not yet completed. Deliberately mutate the protocol to omit cleanup, duplicate a receipt, replay a stale generation, or reclaim a child-owned handle on cancellation: each mutation must be rejected or expose an invariant violation. Include cancellation winning a pending handoff immediately before parent early return. After a model survives, compare tiny compiler fixtures and emitted Go against those transitions. A bounded model would not prove compiler correctness. No model, prototype or benchmark has been run for this proposal.

## Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

This adds syntax, affine obligation checks, a ledger and generated join/cleanup code; it deletes no checker machinery. Inside the opt-in region, fire-and-forget exit and immediate early return are lost, and exit may block forever. Initially reject panic/recover, opaque blocking calls and foreign ownership escapes. No bounded cancellation latency, termination, rollback, exactly-once external effects, deadlock freedom or process-abort recovery is promised. The checker, lowering, ledger and existing release implementation remain trusted. If useful cleanup requires dropping ownership rules or trusting arbitrary foreign code, publish that counterexample and stop.

AI-assisted proposal; source review only. References pinned to `44a08b96dca77e49cf8c6469d8c177ef908b5234`. No commitment to a prototype or measured result.

— Ski

title: [wildcard] Delete the alias graph: make ownership a capability the type carries

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

body:
*Submitted through the API rather than the issue form, so the `wildcard` / `💎 Bounty` labels could not be attached from this account (adding labels needs repo admin rights). Please add them when triaging — the title and the section structure follow the wildcard template.*

---

### The idea, in a paragraph

Delete the alias / may-share graph and make ownership a property the **type**
carries, not a property a whole-body flow analysis reconstructs. Today
`hy-check` decides move/freeze from three mutable side tables per function —
`aliases`, `may_share`, `non_owned_origin`, plus scope snapshots
(`scopes` / `alias_scopes` / `share_scopes`) — and every soundness landing of
the last cycle has been another special case bolted onto them: the #14
scope-aware env, the #31 shadow restoration, #73/#160's `collect_ref_roots`
sweep, #194's `call_local_roots` exemption and its `callee_returns_own_param`
narrowing, #195's may-share sweep in `scope_pop`. The representation is the
defect, not the rule set: `may_share` is a **flow-insensitive
over-approximation of storage identity**, so it is simultaneously too coarse
in one direction (corpus 15's `chunk_of` is a false positive that needs an
exemption to stay accepted) and too coarse in the other (the exemption becomes
the hole: #194 is exactly that exemption applied one level too high). The
proposal: a **linear capability value**. `own T` is a first-class,
non-duplicable type; `share` / `borrow` are explicit type constructors; a
spawn, send, return or store *consumes* the capability in the type system the
way `move` does today, so "is this binding still owned?" becomes a **type**
question answered locally and compositionally instead of a graph question
answered globally and conservatively. No `may_share`, no `alias_scopes`, no
`check_loop_backedge`, no `scope_pop` sweep, no `call_local_roots`.

### Which assumption it breaks

The checker's core premise (SPEC §9.3, GUARANTEES rows 3 and 6): that
ownership is a *dataflow property of bindings inside a body*, recoverable from
an alias/may-share graph plus scope snapshots. This kills the graph, the
snapshots, the loop-backedge pass, and the entire genre of "follow-up gap in
#X" fixes. It also puts pressure on the `.hy` / `.go` split: a capability type
has to survive into the emitted Go surface (a zero-size phantom plus a
`go vet`-visible contract, or it forces the split's first real crack), which
makes this a proposal about the split as well as about the analysis.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

A normal bug-fix bounty optimizes *this* analysis — the ladder pays for
merging, so by construction it cannot accept "delete the analysis". The
evidence that deleting it is the right move is the **shape of the last 72
hours**: at least seven landed soundness fixes are the same rule re-derived on
a representation that keeps leaking — #14, #23, #31, #73, #160, #194, #195 —
and their corpus rows (24, 40/41, 46, 47) are the fossil record. Each one
added a table entry, a snapshot, or an exemption. Meanwhile **the exemptions
are the bug surface**: #194 is precisely the corpus-15 exemption
(`call_local_roots`) keyed on the resolved root instead of the loop-local
binding. The checker also had to grow `non_owned_origin` (O5.1/O5.4) and a
composite carve-out for #188 — three documented "we cannot decide this
structurally, so we special-case it" sites. An analysis that needs a special
case to keep a fresh-copy control accepted, and whose special case is the next
CVE-shaped bug, is telling us the property is not graph-shaped. If "does this
value still have an owner?" were a type, the answer would be available at the
definition site and there would be nothing to sweep, snapshot, or exempt.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

The corpus is already the spec (48 registered programs, `tools/corpus_harness.py`,
`VERDICTS.md`), so this is falsifiable **without a prototype**:

1. **M1 — falsification attempt.** Write the capability-typed surface for the
   corpus's value forms and hand-derive the verdict of every row under it.
   Target 48/48 verdict agreement. If any row's verdict cannot be derived
   without an alias graph, publish *that row* as the wall — the idea dies with
   a learning, which is a paid outcome here.
2. **M2 — the real metric, pre-registered.** The E3001 / E3003 / E3004 / E3006
   / E3101 diagnostic codes must stay **identical on the corpus**, while
   `may_share`, `alias_scopes`, `share_scopes`, `call_local_roots`,
   `check_loop_backedge` and `scope_pop`'s sweeps are **deleted**, and each of
   the three known exemption sites (`call_local_roots`, `non_owned_origin`,
   the #188 composite carve-out) either disappears or is restated as a type
   rule. Binary outcome; no judgment call.
3. **M3 — what would falsify loudly.** If reproducing corpus 15's ACCEPT
   requires reintroducing a flow-insensitive copy of `may_share`, the idea is
   dead in this form, and the learning — "the graph is load-bearing for
   fresh-copy controls" — is worth publishing on its own.

### Cost honesty

This is a rewrite of `hy-check`'s core, not a patch. `model.rs`'s three side
tables and the scope machinery go away; `loans.rs` / `freeze.rs` shrink to
"consume a capability, emit its type error"; the `.hy` surface grows a type
constructor that must be representable in the emitted Go (zero-size phantom +
a `go vet`-visible contract, or the split cracks). It will renumber
diagnostics and it will break the emitter's assumptions about which bindings
need lowering. If the analysis is wrong, the cost is bounded by M1 — and paid
in the currency this track already accepts, a published wall.

### Track terms

- [x] I understand no prototype is required and failure-with-knowledge is a
  valid, paid outcome
- [x] I understand all outcomes (including declines and failures) are
  published in MOONSHOT.md

title: [wildcard] GUARANTEES.md row 12 is wrong: cancellation-safety is a one-pass corollary of Tier-0

body:
## The idea, in a paragraph

Async-cancellation safety ("no checked goroutine can block forever past its cancellation scope") is not a new research program for Hybrid: it is a monotone dataflow pass over information the Tier-0 checker already computes. GUARANTEES.md row 12's "no claim" about context.Context cancellation semantics is a scope choice, not a capability limit. Row 12 should move from "no claim" to a checked-subset cancellation-safety guarantee, leaving `managed` blocks as the single documented cancellation-blind spot — which strengthens, not weakens, the audit story for `managed`.

## Which assumption it breaks

GUARANTEES.md row 12 (context.Context cancellation trees — "Not modeled; the value itself is classified like any other at a check-site. No claim about cancellation semantics — the claim is about value sharing, not protocol liveness"), answering MOONSHOT.md solicitation prompt #4 ("Impossible guarantees": deadlock-freedom, async-cancellation, ...). The sacred cow: Tier-0 is a value-sharing checker only; protocol-liveness properties are declared out of scope (row 16 does the same for send-on-closed panic). The contrarian claim: one liveness property is already within reach, because the checker already reasons about the structures that decide it.

## Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

Because it reclassifies a documented "impossible" as engineering. The four premises already exist in the spec/checker:

1. **Spawn graph is finite and visible.** Exactly two Hybrid-level check-sites (task spawn, channel send) gate cross-task sharing (SPEC-LANGUAGE.md 8.4, C5). Every goroutine in the emitted Go originates at a checked site. No hidden spawns in checked code.
2. **Cancellation tokens cannot leak past function scope.** Loans are function-local, created and dying inside one function body (SPEC-LANGUAGE.md 9 / O2, the no-visible-lifetimes promise). A ctx-derived borrow (e.g. a channel tied to a context) that survives function exit is already representable as a loan-liveness violation — not a new analysis.
3. **Fail-closed on the unknown.** Anything the checker cannot resolve is rejected (HYB-E3005, rule FC, O4.9 — the fail-closed boundary), never silently blessed. Foreign/unknown cancellation trees are compile errors, not blind spots. The only cancellation-blind region is `managed` blocks — already linted, counted, and CI-gated (GUARANTEES row 8).
4. **Blocking sites are enumerable per function body.** Channel receive, select, and (inside managed) mutex ops are syntactically finite per body. The proposed check: every blocking site in checked code must be dominated by a cancellation-observable signal reachable from a check-site-known context. This is the same shape as the existing E31xx loan-conflict analysis (Polonius-style dataflow, 9.1/O15) — one more monotone pass, not new machinery.

A normal feature bounty would reject "give us cancellation semantics" as scope creep. The contrarian case is that it is not creep — it is one more monotone pass on existing machinery.

## How we would know it works (or doesn't)

The falsifier: one accepted .hy program, using only checked code (no `managed`, no foreign Go), in which the current checker accepts a task that blocks forever on a channel operation after its context is cancelled — a cancellation-oblivious blocking shape the proposed dominance check cannot name. Publish the falsifier-hunt call: if such a program is found, the proposal dies publicly and the checker corpus gains a regression case (failure-with-knowledge = M2 still pays). If no such program survives adversarial review, row 12 falls. Milestones: M1 accepted ($250) -> falsifier-hunt call published, 2 weeks -> M2 learning published with corpus results, 4 weeks ($250). What changes if accepted: row 12 moves from "no claim" to a checked-subset cancellation-safety guarantee; the differential loop gains ~5 cancellation corpus cases.

## Cost honesty

Honest about what this is: an argument, not a machine-checked proof — drafted without running the checker (no Rust/Go toolchain available to me), so the falsifier hunt needs the maintainer's toolchain. Scoped to the checked subset only; `managed` blocks and foreign Go stay outside, exactly as today. Cost: one dataflow pass reusing the 9.1 machinery + ~5 corpus programs. No new crates, no spec rewrite. If the AI maintainer produces one accepted cancellation-oblivious program, the proposal is dead — and that is a valid, paid outcome under the Wildcard rules.

- [x] I understand no prototype is required and failure-with-knowledge is a valid, paid outcome
- [x] I understand all outcomes (including declines and failures) are published in MOONSHOT.md

# [wildcard] Erase the `.hy` / `.go` Split: Whole-Package Tier-0 Checking via Native Go AST and Export-Data Analysis

### The idea, in a paragraph

Hybrid's foundational thesis is *"Keep Go exactly as it is. Add Rust where you need it"* (`SPEC-LANGUAGE.md`), yet its current implementation directly contradicts this by forcing a bifurcated two-file world: `.hy` files parsed by a custom Rust frontend (`compiler/crates/hy-syntax`) and emitted back to Go via a custom code generator (`compiler/crates/hy-emit`). Because `hy-check` operates as a single-file syntactic abstract interpreter (`check_file(&File)` in `compiler/crates/hy-check/src/lib.rs:88`), it has zero visibility into declarations in sibling `.go` files in the same package. Any type defined in Go falls back to `TypeShape::Unknown` (`compiler/crates/hy-check/src/shape.rs:56`), which under O4.9 (rule FC) triggers fail-closed rejection `HYB-E3005` at every `task` spawn or channel send. We propose **erasing the `.hy` file extension and AST translation pipeline entirely**. Hybrid becomes a **Go-native toolchain extension (a whole-package Analyzer or `toolexec` compiler pass)** operating directly on standard Go AST and Go package export data (`go/types`). Tier-0 ownership, loans, and sendability semantics are attached directly to standard Go syntax via compiler directives (`//hy:check`, `//hy:managed`) and zero-cost phantom intrinsics (`hy.Move()`, `hy.Task()`), deleting `hy-syntax`, `hy-emit`, and the fragile hardcoded `foreign.rs` stub table while giving developers 100% native compatibility with `gopls`, `go build`, and standard Go tooling.

### Which assumption it breaks

This proposal directly answers **Solicitation Prompt 1** in `MOONSHOT.md` (*"Kill the `.hy` / `.go` split. Whole-module checking, or checking that attaches to ordinary Go via annotations — what would it take, and what guarantee dies with it?"*) and attacks three sacred cows:

1. **Sacred Cow #1 — That Hybrid must be a distinct surface language with bespoke grammar, file extension (`.hy`), and a parallel parser.**
   `SPEC-LANGUAGE.md §1.1 (LX4)` normatively documents that Hybrid diverges from Go in only three cosmetic surface tokens: `fn` vs `func`, `pub` vs uppercase export, and `match` vs `switch`. Maintaining ~9,500 lines of Rust in `compiler/crates/hy-syntax` and `compiler/crates/hy-emit` just to translate these three keywords forces Hybrid into an endless treadmill of re-implementing Go features (e.g. range-over-func, generics, type sets) and duplicate buildability rules (`compiler/crates/hy-check/src/buildable.rs`, issue #134).
2. **Sacred Cow #2 — That `hy-check` is an isolated, single-file AST walk.**
   Today, `compiler/crates/hyb/src/main.rs:474-512` requires sibling `.go` files to exist on disk just to extract a `package <name>` clause (`HYB-E9002`), yet `hy-check` ignores those sibling files completely. A struct declared in a sibling `.go` file cannot cross a concurrency boundary in `.hy` without a manual `managed` escape or duplicate declaration. Whole-package checking breaks the single-file walk assumption and checks packages compositionally using Go's own export data.
3. **Sacred Cow #3 — The Physical File Safety Perimeter (GUARANTEES.md lines 14–30).**
   Today, the boundary is physical: code inside `.hy` is checked; code inside `.go` is an unverified foreign realm where "Go-API escapes follow Go's DRF-SC memory model with `go test -race` as the backstop" (`GUARANTEES.md` row 9).
   **The guarantee that dies (honest trade-off):** In a unified `.go` world, the closed-world lexical ban on `go func()` and raw pointers (`SPEC-LANGUAGE.md §1.1`) cannot be globally enforced across an entire Go project. The safety guarantee shifts from a *file-level physical sandbox* to an *annotated function/package boundary*. Un-annotated Go functions within the package are treated as an explicit ambient `managed` perimeter.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

A standard feature bounty is constrained to fixing incremental holes in `foreign.rs` or patching AST visitor quirks in `walk.rs`. That approach cannot solve the architectural blind spots:

- **Eliminates the `foreign.rs` hardcoded barrier:** Today, `compiler/crates/hy-check/src/foreign.rs` maintains a hardcoded table of 16 packages (`BUILTIN_PACKAGES`, lines 22–38) and hand-curated `CallMode` descriptors (`Produce`, `Borrow`, `Mutate`, `Consume`, lines 41–55). Lines 3–16 of `foreign.rs` explicitly classify this as tech debt. Any 3rd-party Go module, or unmodeled standard library type (like `sync.Pool` or `atomic.Pointer`), degrades to `TypeShape::Unknown` and fails closed (`HYB-E3005`). By analyzing standard Go AST against `go/types` export data, the checker resolves the exact structural shape of *every* imported Go type and sibling declaration automatically.
- **Deletes duplicate compiler machinery:** Eliminates `compiler/crates/hy-syntax` (~6,000 LOC), `compiler/crates/hy-emit` (~3,500 LOC), and the synchronization pass in `compiler/crates/hy-check/src/buildable.rs` (which had to re-implement Go's unused-variable and short-declaration rules in Rust to prevent emitting unbuildable Go).
- **Zero-Friction Developer & Tooling Integration:** Eliminates generated `*.hy.go` files and `gofmt` subprocess piping (`compiler/crates/hyb/src/main.rs:772`). Developers edit ordinary `.go` files: `gopls` provides instant jump-to-definition, autocompletion, and refactoring without a pre-generation step; debuggers (`delve`) map directly to human-written lines without sourcemap skew.
- **Differentiation from #174 and #175:** Proposal #174 tries to offload proofs to `cmd/compile` using CPS-nested phantom wrappers in emitted Go (increasing emit complexity and ruining readable Go output); Proposal #175 replaces loans with affine capability tokens inside the isolated `hy-check` engine. Neither touches the `.hy`/`.go` file wall. This proposal kills the file split at the root, making Hybrid a zero-overhead safety analyzer for the Go ecosystem.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

**Milestone 1 ($250) — Corpus Parity on Native Go AST (Soundness Validation):**
1. Translate all 46 test cases in `tests/checker-corpus/` (all 33 REJECT fixtures and all 13 ACCEPT / ACCEPT-MANAGED fixtures) into standard `.go` files with inline directives:
   - Function boundaries marked with `//hy:check`.
   - Moves expressed as zero-cost generic intrinsic `hy.Move(&x)` (which expands to nothing at runtime).
   - Tasks spawned via `hy.Task(f, args...)` or `//hy:task go f(args...)`.
   - Map-slot loans expressed via `hy.Borrow(&m[k])` or scoped lexical helper.
2. Implement an experimental driver (either in Go via `golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis` or in Rust via `go/parser` JSON bridge) executing Tier-0 analysis (`sendability.rs`, `freeze.rs`, `loans.rs`) over Go AST and `go/types`.
3. *Falsification Gate for M1:*
   - The Go-native checker must achieve **100% verdict parity** against the 46 pre-registered corpus cases: all 33 REJECT cases must be rejected with their pre-registered diagnostics, and all 13 ACCEPT / ACCEPT-MANAGED cases must pass.
   - If any core Tier-0 guarantee (e.g. A1b use-after-move, A1c loop backedge move, A3 map slot loan invalidation) cannot be soundly expressed or enforced on Go's AST without requiring semantic changes to Go's runtime, M1 fails and the post-mortem documents the exact syntactic limit.

**Milestone 2 ($250) — Multi-File Sibling Resolution & Usability Ceiling Report:**
1. Benchmark multi-file package analysis: Construct a 10-fixture suite where checked functions consume structs, methods, and channels declared in sibling `.go` files. Demonstrate that sibling types resolve to concrete `TypeShape::Struct` rather than `TypeShape::Unknown`, passing `task` spawn checks without `HYB-E3005` or manual `managed` annotations.
2. Compile-time performance measurement: Measure the wall-clock compilation overhead of `hyb (Analyzer) + go build` versus the current multi-stage pipeline (`hy-syntax parse` + `hy-check` + `hy-emit` + `run_gofmt` + `go build`).
3. *Published Learning Deliverable:*
   Publish a comprehensive post-mortem to `MOONSHOT.md`:
   - If successful: The roadmap for retiring `hy-syntax` and `hy-emit`, making Hybrid an idiomatic `go vet` toolchain extension.
   - If failed: An evidence-backed analysis detailing exactly why Go's native AST or evaluation order prevents sound borrow-checking (e.g. unconstrained pointer aliasing across package variables, or inability to distinguish value-copy from reference-copy without whole-program escape analysis), defining the theoretical necessity of the `.hy` language barrier.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

- **What gets deleted:**
  - `compiler/crates/hy-syntax/` (lexer, parser, AST: ~6,000 LOC).
  - `compiler/crates/hy-emit/` (Go code emitter: ~3,500 LOC).
  - `compiler/crates/hy-check/src/buildable.rs` (~600 LOC of duplicated Go variable validation).
  - `compiler/crates/hy-check/src/foreign.rs` (hardcoded package stubs).
  - Eliminates `HYB-E9002` (the requirement for a sibling `.go` file just to extract package names).
- **What gets rewritten:**
  - The checker's frontend switches from consuming `hy_syntax::File` to consuming Go AST (via `go/ast` export JSON or a native Go implementation of `hy-check`).
  - AST nodes in `walk.rs`, `loans.rs`, and `freeze.rs` map from `hy_syntax` nodes to standard Go AST node equivalents (`ast.FuncDecl`, `ast.AssignStmt`, `ast.GoStmt`).
- **Surface changes for users:**
  - Users write idiomatic Go (`func`, `switch`, exported capitalized identifiers) instead of Hybrid's `fn`, `match`, and `pub`.
  - For sum types and pattern matching (`SPEC-LANGUAGE.md §2.5`), code relies on standard Go sealed interfaces and type switches rather than Hybrid's custom `match` expression.
- **Migration path:**
  - A 100-line mechanical migration script (`hy2go`) translates existing `.hy` files in `examples/` and `tests/` into standard `.go` files with `//hy:check` annotations and `hy.Move()` intrinsics.

title: [wildcard] Generate closed channel protocols from one global program to make deadlock freedom achievable

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

For a new, explicitly closed subset, make the global communication program the source of truth and generate every participant's Go endpoint from it. Today each goroutine independently decides when to send/receive; the ownership checker cannot establish the resulting protocol's progress. Instead, a finite global description says which role communicates with which role and where choices occur. Projection generates both ends, communicates branch choices, keeps the raw channels private, and joins every participant before returning ordinary values. Aim for **communication-deadlock freedom within that closed protocol**, conditional on terminating local computation and fair scheduling. This directly answers MOONSHOT prompt 4; it does not extend the claim to arbitrary Go, foreign callbacks, cancellation, or all existing `.hy` programs.

### Which assumption it breaks

The assumption that user-authored goroutines and ambient Go channels must remain the primary source language for checked concurrency. The design deliberately replaces them inside the new subset with a global program. GUARANTEES.md currently declines deadlock/liveness guarantees and row 16 declines send/close ordering. Those limits remain honest for today's language; this proposes a separately identified stronger contract, rather than relabelling existing acceptance as proof.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

Ownership and correct endpoint types do not solve composition. Consider two unbuffered channels, with these local traces:

```text
A: send p; receive q
B: send q; receive p
```

Each channel separately has a sender and a receiver. The combined program still blocks immediately: both first operations are sends. Adding phantom endpoint states alone does not discharge this global obligation. A single projectable global program can rule out the incompatible ordering before generating Go.

The proposed change is therefore to the programming model: generate participants from one communication plan instead of repairing independently authored participants. It retains plain-Go output and the existing ownership checks for payloads. It is an application of established work, not a claim that session types or choreography are new: [Ng and Yoshida, CC 2016](https://nickng.io/publications/go-synthesis/main.pdf) infer session descriptions and synthesize global graphs for Go; [Carbone and Montesi, POPL 2013](https://www.fabriziomontesi.com/files/cm13.pdf) study deadlock-free endpoint generation from global programs. Neither paper verifies a future Hybrid implementation.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

Proposed analysis milestones, subject to maintainer acceptance:

1. **Write the boundary and operational rules first.** Start with a fixed finite participant set, unbuffered private channels, finite communication sequences and projectable labelled choices. No dynamic spawn, endpoint delegation, raw `close`, nil channels, `select`, locks, cancellation or opaque foreign calls. Local computation must be from an explicitly total, nonblocking subset; purity alone is insufficient. Endpoint values must not escape through returns, closures, containers or foreign APIs. Unproven effects/escapes reject.
2. **Try to break composition before growing syntax.** Enumerate the complete reachable state spaces of bounded two- and three-role models. Pre-register passing request/reply, a three-stage pipeline, finite fan-out/fan-in and an announced choice. Mutations must reject or exhibit a witness: both-send, both-receive, the cross-session cycle above, an unannounced nonlocal branch, and an escaped endpoint. Check absence of reachable nonterminal stuck states and progress of every unfinished participant, not just existence of one runnable task. Exhaustive bounded results are evidence for those models, not an unbounded theorem.
3. **Only if the model survives, test projection.** Generate ordinary Go for the accepted cases; compare observable traces/results with the global model, and deliberately corrupt endpoint ordering to show the independent checker rejects it. The old corpus and its weaker guarantee must remain unchanged. Publish the smallest counterexample or an explicit simulation/progress argument; no claim ships solely because a few runs finish or `-race` stays quiet.

### Cost honesty

This adds a new source construct, projection machinery, an effects/escape boundary and diagnostics. Many familiar Go patterns are excluded initially. There is no promised zero-cost runtime, cancellation safety, arbitrary-program termination, solver speed or compatibility with opaque callbacks. State-space growth and unusably restrictive computation rules are explicit reasons to stop. A negative result would explain precisely which useful protocol cannot be expressed or which emitted trace violates the model. The finite model below has been run; I have not implemented this compiler change, proved an unbounded theorem or measured compiler/runtime performance.

### Bounded model evidence

[Executable Python model, actual output and reproduction notes](https://gist.github.com/elliotthugftgo86r66/0c4592509bd7e03db8365250620bb9f6). Eleven example/guard assertions pass: three positive protocols, five concrete deadlocks, one incomplete-exploration result (`unknown`), and two unsupported-input rejections.

The useful distinction is observable: request/reply explores three states and completes, while reversing one endpoint's order deadlocks immediately. An announced three-role choice has eight reachable states without deadlock. Removing the announcement and allowing an independent choice produces sixteen reachable states, including **two deadlocked states and a completing path**. One successful run would therefore miss this protocol defect.

These are exhaustive results for the supplied finite acyclic graphs only. The model does not parse Hybrid, check effects or escapes in actual source, generate Go, model payload ownership, or establish a future projection's correctness. Its resource limit returns `unknown`, never a safety verdict. No Go build, full compiler suite or runtime measurement is claimed.

### Track terms

- [x] I understand that no prototype is required and a selected failure-with-knowledge can earn the track's learning milestone.
- [x] I understand that outcomes, including declines and failures, are published in MOONSHOT.md.

Prepared with Codex assistance. Submitted for the Wildcard Track's review; selection, acceptance and any payout remain the maintainer's decision. No award or payment is claimed.

title: [wildcard] Zero-Checker Emit: Offload Tier-0 Ownership, Freeze, and Loan Proofs to cmd/compile via CPS-Scoped Phantom Witnesses

labels.name: 💎 Bounty
labels.description: $500 Hybrid Bounty pool, see BOUNTY.md. Payouts ride the top-10 ladder.

body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Instead of maintaining a growing abstract interpreter in Rust (hy-check's flat walk, scope-event replay, may_share graph, and hand-curated  oreign.rs tables) and then erasing all ownership information when emitting Go (hy-emit), **emit ownership, freeze states, and loan windows directly into Go's static type system using zero-sized phantom capability tokens (struct{}) and continuation-scoped lexical shadowing**. Every non-sendable binding x of type T is paired in emitted Go with a zero-byte capability witness hyCap_x of type hyLive[/*root*/]. A transfer site (	ask f(move x) or ch <- move x) opens a lexical continuation scope for the remainder of the block that shadows hyCap_x := hyMoved{}, while every emitted read, write, loop-backedge tail, and alias access emits a zero-cost type assertion hyUse(hyCap_x) requiring hyLive. cmd/compile itself then rejects use-after-move (HYB-E3003), loop-backedge double-move, and .hy↔.go boundary mismatches at go build time with zero runtime allocation or register overhead.

### Which assumption it breaks

It attacks **three sacred cows simultaneously** (Solicitation Prompts **#2**, **#1**, and **#3** in MOONSHOT.md):

1. **Sacred Cow #1 — That hy-check must prove ownership in Rust before hy-emit erases it.** Today hy-check (walk.rs, loans.rs,  reeze.rs, sendability.rs, closures.rs) duplicates scope resolution, type-shape inference, and control-flow flattening that cmd/compile already performs on the emitted Go. Every mismatch between hy-check's flat walk and Go's actual semantics has produced a P0 soundness bug (#14 lexical shadowing, #27 shallow-copy may_share, #38 call-returned alias, #48 multi-value unpack shapes, #57 method/fn table collision, #60 non-owned move).
2. **Sacred Cow #2 — That hy-emit must emit flat, line-for-line Go statements (stmt.rs) with ownership erased.** Under this proposal, move and borrow-loan bindings are **scope-opening binders** in emitted Go: statements following move x sit inside a nested { hyCap_x := hyMoved{}; ... } block, and loop bodies end with a static backedge witness ar _ hyLive[root] = hyCap_x before the closing } (and before every continue).
3. **Sacred Cow #3 — The .hy / .go boundary wall and  oreign.rs hand-curated tables.** Because hyMoved / hyLive / hyLoan are ordinary Go generic phantom types (struct{}), native .go functions can declare borrow vs. consume contracts directly in their Go signatures ( unc Consume[R any](v T, cap hyLive[R]) hyMoved), killing the blind spot where hy-check must either maintain a hardcoded  oreign.rs table or fail closed (HYB-E3005).

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

A normal feature PR can only patch the next edge case in hy-check (walk.rs / loans.rs /  reeze.rs). That is an infinite treadmill: as Hybrid adds enum payloads, generics, methods, and multi-file packages, hy-check is forced to evolve into a full second Go typechecker just to figure out whether two bindings might alias mutable GC storage.

Offloading the proof to cmd/compile inverts the architecture:
- **Type-directed sharing comes from Go's real types for free:** If m2 := m or s2 := s (where s is a struct carrying a reference field), emitting hyCap_m2 := &hyCap_m (or tying both bindings to the same root phantom type parameter R) means invalidating the root capability on move invalidates the entire sharing component in cmd/compile.
- **Cross-file and .hy↔.go checking becomes compositional:** A .go package no longer needs an entry in compiler/crates/hy-check/src/foreign.rs to participate in A2/A3/A7 loan and consume checking; Go's own package export data carries the capability signature across package boundaries.
- **Zero runtime cost:** Go's compiler (cmd/compile) completely erases struct{} values and inlines trivial generic witness functions ( unc hyRequireLive[R any](hyLive[R]) {}), producing byte-for-byte identical machine code and zero heap escapes (-gcflags=-m).

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

We can falsify or validate this without touching production hy-check by running a **pre-registered 24-case experiment against 	ests/checker-corpus/**:

1. **Milestone 1 (M1 — Specification & Encoding Matrix):**
   Write out the exact Go type encoding for the five core Tier-0 invariants:
   - **A1b (post-move use):** lexical continuation block { hyCap_x := hyMoved{}; ... } after move x.
   - **A1c (loop-backedge move):** emitted tail witness ar _ hyLive[xRoot] = hyCap_x at the end of every  or/loop body and before every continue.
   - **A2/A3 (borrow loan window):** loan token hyLoan_x live from borrow call to last use, with mutations requiring hyRequireUnloaned(hyCap_x).
   - **#27 (may_share alias group):** shared root phantom tag R across   := a so moving either requires consuming the shared capability.
   - **A5 / #60 (non-owned move of params/receivers/captures):** parameters, method receivers, and closure captures bind hyBorrowed[R] rather than hyLive[R], so hyRequireOwnedForMove(hyCap_p) fails in cmd/compile.

2. **Milestone 2 (M2 — Corpus Falsification & Join-Point Wall Report):**
   Test the encoding against all 24 files in 	ests/checker-corpus/ using go build alone (with hy-check bypassed) and publish the exact boundary where pure lexical Go shadowing succeeds vs. hits a wall:
   - **Hypothesis to test:** Pure lexical shadowing in Go handles straight-line moves, nested-scope uses, non-owned parameters/receivers/captures, and loop-tail backedges, **but hits a fundamental control-flow join wall on conditional moves inside child branches** (e.g., if cond { task w(move x) } followed by a use of x *after* the if block closes, because a lexical shadow { hyCap_x := hyMoved{} } inside the 	hen-brace pops at } unless the post-if statements are CPS-duplicated or hoisted into an outer state type).
   - **Deliverable:** A self-contained table mapping all 24 	ests/checker-corpus/ cases and GUARANTEES.md rows 1–12 to *(a) proven by cmd/compile via lexical witness*, *(b) proven by cmd/compile only with CPS branch tail-duplication (and its code-size cost)*, or *(c) impossible in Go's type system without hy-check*, plus go build -gcflags=-m escape-analysis verification confirming zero runtime allocation overhead.

### Cost honesty (optional but powerful)

- **Emitted Go readability after move degrades:** Opening a continuation block { hyCap_x := hyMoved{}; ... } after each move indents the remainder of the function by one level per move, and handling conditional moves across if/match join points without hy-check requires either CPS tail-duplication or keeping a tiny join-point liveness pass in hy-check.
- **Diagnostic mapping (HYB-E3001..E3006):** Raw cmd/compile errors say cannot use hyCap_x (variable of type hyMoved) as hyLive; preserving Hybrid's rustc-style HYB-E3003 diagnostics requires either a thin error-parser over go build output (keyed by struct tags/type names like hyMoved_line_42) or running the Go typechecker (go/types) as an oracle rather than deleting hy-check's diagnostic formatter.
- **Even if we do not delete hy-check:** The encoding immediately serves as a **second, independent soundness oracle in 	ools/differential_loop.py** — any .hy program accepted by hy-check whose witness-encoded Go fails go build is an automatic, zero-human-effort discovery of a P0 soundness bug in hy-check.

body:
### The idea, in a paragraph

Replace path-sensitive, per-binding syntactic alias/loan/freeze analysis across `freeze.rs` and `closures.rs` with Linear Region Capabilities (`Cap[R]`) and Type-Colored Sub-Graphs. Within a task holding a region token `r : Cap[R]`, arbitrary Go aliasing is 100% legal without false positives (`HYB-E3001`/`E3004`). Cross-task transfer moves the single non-copyable capability `r`, rendering all caller-local bindings statically inert. This eliminates the entire whack-a-mole game of statement-walk alias tracking (`st.aliases`, `st.may_share`, `call_local_roots`, closure re-assign bypasses).

### Which assumption it breaks

Attacks Solicitation #2 ("Replace the borrow-checker machinery. Capability tokens, linear-type encodings inside Go's type system, runtime-enforced ownership — anything that deletes the alias/loan/freeze analysis rather than extending it."). Kills the sacred cow that Hybrid can soundly deduce exclusive ownership of arbitrary Go GC reference graphs (map, []T, *T) via AST statement-walk heuristics. As proved by the relentless stream of P0 soundness bugs in the repo (#14, #27, #38, #48, #54, #60, #137, #301), syntactic path-sensitive alias tracking cannot converge because aliasing in Go is a property of heap subgraphs, not local variable names.

### Why this is a breakthrough, not an increment

Instead of incrementally patching `freeze.rs` and `closures.rs` for every new expression, control flow join, loop back-edge, or closure re-assignment, this completely deletes ~1,200+ LOC of brittle AST dataflow machinery. It trades syntactic whack-a-mole for a simple 1-bit linear capability check (`Cap[R]`), enabling arbitrary idiomatic Go aliasing inside a region while providing absolute compile-time safety across task boundaries.

### How we would know it works (or doesn't)

- Milestone 1 (Acceptance & Encoding): Encode the 24+ existing corpus test cases (including shadowing, multi-value assigns, closures, and loop back-edges) under Region-Brand typing (`In[R, T]`).
- Falsification Criteria: Falsified on ergonomics if >20% of idiomatic `.hy` accept-corpus programs require explicit manual region wiring that cannot be inferred via anonymous per-allocation region brands (`Cap[$alloc_id]`). **Goals**
- Establish a baseline benchmark suite for all platform API endpoints
- Measure latency (p50, p95, p99), throughput (req/s), and error rate under load
- Identify bottlenecks before they surface in production
- Produce a reproducible report that can be re-run on future builds for regression tracking

**Scope**
- [ ] All endpoints under `/api/` are included in the benchmark suite
